paragraphs: Here's what hit me, friend. Samuel reminds the people that God brought Israel out of Egypt and rescued them from "all the kingdoms that oppressed you" (1 Samuel 10:18). Then he says they have rejected the God who "saves you from all your troubles and afflictions" (1 Samuel 10:19). They already had the Rescuer, and they asked for a king anyway. So the big question is the same one we all face: who do we trust to save us?

Now look at the man they got. The LORD chose Saul, and the people shout, "Long live the king!" (1 Samuel 10:24). But some worthless men ask, "How can this man save us?" (1 Samuel 10:27). Notice that the question these men ask is the very one Samuel already answered. The people were looking for a savior in a man, and the LORD had been their Savior the whole time.

So here's the takeaway for your own kitchen, baker. Anything we lean on for rescue, a boss, a bank account, a plan, a leader, will be human, and humans have limits. Even the one God chose was found hiding among the baggage (1 Samuel 10:22). Trust the God who saves, because He is the one who has never needed rescuing himself. And I'm telling you, this king's story is not over yet.
